items.name: Certificate provider, models & validity helper
items.description: ICertificateProvider over /certificates, the request/response models, and a pure helper that maps an expiry date to valid / expiring-soon / expired.
acceptance: src/resources/provider/certificate/Certificate.provider.ts extends HttpRequest, sets urlPrefix, exports default; methods list, create, byWorker
Models under src/models/{request,response}/certificate/ per model-conventions.md
ECertificateStatus: VALID | EXPIRING_SOON | EXPIRED
certificateStatus(expiryDate, now) helper using the Dayjs util in Asia/Bangkok; the expiring-soon window is a single named constant
Unit tests at the boundaries: expiry yesterday, today, threshold-1 day, threshold day, threshold+1 day
./init.sh green
items.notes: DONE. certificateStatus(expiryDate, now) — both params required, no internal clock read. CERTIFICATE_EXPIRING_SOON_DAYS = 30, DEFAULTED not confirmed by a product owner — still needs a decision. TIMEZONE: expiryDate is a bare business date parsed with dayjs.tz(str, Asia/Bangkok); now is a real instant parsed with dayjs(now).tz(Asia/Bangkok). The agent proved with a probe run under TZ=America/Los_Angeles, UTC and Asia/Bangkok that a naive single-branch version breaks on a non-UTC host — the two-helper split is load-bearing, do not collapse it.

items.name: Certificate gate on permit submission
items.description: Wire certificate validity into the permit wizard: workers with a missing or expired certificate block submission, and a server CERT_EXPIRED response routes the user back to fix it.
acceptance: Wizard step 4 shows each registered worker's certificate state; a missing or expired cert marks that worker as blocking
Next from step 4 and Submit from step 6 are both blocked while any registered worker's certificate is missing or expired; the blocking worker is named
Step 6's 'Worker certificates valid & not expired' green row reflects the real check, not a hardcoded ✓
A CERT_EXPIRED response from POST /permits/:id/submit returns the user to step 4 with the offending worker highlighted — the server verdict wins over the client check
The Inspector-side CERT_BLOCKED field-entry denial is NOT built here — different repo
./init.sh green
items.notes: This item spans two modules. Update both docs/modules/certificate/ and docs/modules/permit/ progress notes when it lands.
items.evidence: 2026-08-23. Bullets 3/4 were ALREADY SATISFIED by prior work and are unchanged here: PMT-009's `useCertificatePreflight` (Step6Review.vue) already drove the real 'Worker certificates valid & not expired' row off GET /certificates/worker/:name, and the backend's feat-010 pass already had submitDraft() extract `certificateFailures[]` off a rejected POST /permits/:id/submit (SubmitErrorRouting.ts) and route back to step 4 with the offending worker highlighted (Step4PpeWorkers.vue's `serverRejectedCertificates`) — the server's verdict already won over any client guess. Bullets 1/2 (a live client-side gate on step 4/6, before submit) were NOT built and are what this item added: `useCertificatePreflight` gained a debounce-safe sequence token so a stale (superseded) lookup can never overwrite a newer one's verdict — the exact JSA-dead-end failure class PROMPT-LOG warns against; `useWizard` hoisted ONE shared instance (debounced on the `workers` array reference, immediate on mount, local `certificateChecking` loading flag so it never drives the global spinner) so step 4's gate and step 6's row can never disagree; `isNextBlocked`/`canSubmit` now also gate on a CONFIRMED `certificateState === 'fail'` only — never 'loading'/'unknown', so an unresolved lookup can never be stricter than the server; Step4PpeWorkers.vue got a per-worker certificate badge column plus a named-worker blocking list (mirrors the existing server-rejected list); Step6Review.vue now reads `certificateState`/`certificateProblems` as props instead of owning its own instance (same behavior, one source of truth). Bullet 5 is a negative acceptance (Inspector-side CERT_BLOCKED denial) — out of scope by design, not built, nothing to verify. New test: src/tests/pages/permit/create/composables/useWizard.certificatePreflight.test.ts (4 tests) — blocks Next + names the worker on a missing cert, unblocks on a valid cert, never blocks on an unresolved lookup, and proves the staleness guard (a stale 'missing' resolving after a newer 'pass' does not flip Next back to blocked). ./init.sh: ALL GREEN — typecheck PASS, lint PASS, vitest 48 files / 450 tests PASS, live smoke 16/16 PASS against localhost:3000. node ../scripts/check-contract-sync.mjs: OK — openapi in sync, 25 backend error codes all declared, /api/v1 prefix present. bunx eslint / bunx vue-tsc --noEmit clean on every touched file.

items.name: Certificate detail page
items.description: A page at /certificates/:id showing one certificate, reachable by making CertificateCard navigable. Renders the server's `expired` verdict via the existing certificateStatus() helper, and the attachment as a link resolved through GET /file at click time.
acceptance: /certificates/:id renders worker name, role, cert type, issued and expiry dates, and the status badge
The badge comes from certificateStatus()/ECertificateStatus — no second expiry calculation anywhere on the page
`expired` is read from the server's per-row flag; the client only layers the advisory expiring-soon window on top
CertificateCard becomes navigable to this page; it has no click handler or RouterLink today
A certificate WITH filePath shows a link that opens the file through GET /file with the path URL-encoded (storage keys contain slashes — GAPS row 21)
A certificate WITHOUT filePath keeps today's dashed 'No file attached' placeholder, with no broken link and no empty anchor
A directly-typed /certificates/:id belonging to another contractor is refused by the API and the page handles it — list scoping does not protect a typed URL
./init.sh green

items.name: Repoint the certificate write paths at worker identity
items.description: wayfinder 060 landed backend-first and broke every certificate WRITE path in this app. Repoints them at `workerId`: ICertificate (+workerId, −role), both payload models, Certificate.provider including byWorker → /worker/{workerId}, AddCertificate.schema, the three certificate forms, and the two display sites that rendered `certificate.role`. Adds the worker model, provider and a shared WorkerPicker. NOT wayfinder 061-063 — no worker directory, and Step 4 is untouched.
acceptance: ICertificate carries workerId; `role` is gone (it describes the person and moved to Worker)
Create and update payloads send workerId; neither accepts workerName or role
byWorker takes a number and hits /certificates/worker/{workerId} — the name-keyed route was an unscoped cross-tenant read
src/components/worker/WorkerPicker.vue: search, select, inline create, and adopt the workerId carried by a 409 WORKER_ALREADY_EXISTS
All three certificate forms use the picker; none has a role field
useCertificatePreflight checks only rows that carry a workerId, and reports 'unknown' for the rest rather than claiming a pass
./init.sh green
items.notes: Two traps for whoever takes 063. (1) WorkerPicker is a component, not an <input>, so @primevue/forms never sees its value — the form needs a hidden input registering `workerId` or submit silently no-ops. (2) Build the payload from `formData`, not from the Form's emitted `values`: mixing the two sources is how this sent `undefined` after the picker landed. Reuse WorkerPicker rather than writing a second autocomplete; per the other session, 063 also needs inline-create-asking-role-only, which it already does.
